nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Keep the reproduction prerequisites nonfatal.

If Setup Go, Capture GOROOT, or Start DIFC Proxy fails, Actions skips the agent rather than continuing ordinary triage without reproduction. Only the later preparation step has continue-on-error. Make prerequisite failures skip reproduction without aborting triage or bypassing the proxy, through the workflow source/compiler configuration, then regenerate the lock file.

nodes.body: Go and security-proxy bootstrap remain required. I narrowed the best-effort wording to the helper's individual build and download failures rather than bypassing those prerequisites. I haven't implemented ordinary-triage fallback for bootstrap failure, so I'm leaving this open.

nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Do not identify the selected workflow ref as the default-branch build.

A manual dispatch against a feature branch checks out that branch because the generated checkout has no explicit ref, but this function labels its build as trunk. The agent can consequently report a fix as present on the default branch when it exists only on the dispatched branch. Build cli/cli's default branch separately, or identify this as the selected source snapshot in both the build label and agent instructions.

nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Do not describe Git operations as unsupported.

The backend now supports real Git fixtures through ghmock repo/git/write and runs each build in an independent workspace with --in. Listing Git operations as something ghmock cannot cover tells triage to omit the relevant part of reports such as linked-worktree or repo-sync failures, even though the helper can reproduce it. Please direct the agent to those fixture commands and reserve the exception for genuinely unsupported dependencies such as an OS keyring.

nodes.body:
🛑 Requirement: Export a portable archive before uploading the evidence.

The staging upload omits hidden files, so a directory export loses its .git metadata; its absolute worktree links also become invalid after download. Maintainers therefore cannot reliably inspect the saved Git/worktree state. Use ghmock's archive export to preserve hidden metadata, permissions, and portable worktree links.
